---
title: "Few-shot Learning"
description: "A learning setting where a model must generalize to a task or class from only a small number of examples."
term: "Few-shot Learning"
letter: "F"
category: "Machine Learning"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Few-shot learning aims to make useful predictions for a new task or class
after seeing only a few labeled examples. It is especially relevant when
collecting labels is expensive.

## Technical explanation

Few-shot methods use prior training across tasks, pretrained
representations, metric learning, meta-learning, or in-context examples
to adapt from limited supervision. The term covers multiple problem
setups, and evaluation must separate classes or tasks appropriately to
measure genuine transfer.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Many domains have scarce labels for rare or emerging categories. Few-shot
approaches can reduce annotation needs, but performance may vary sharply
with example selection, domain shift, and the similarity between training
and target tasks.

## How it works

The system first acquires transferable knowledge from data or pretraining.
For a new task, it uses a small support set to adapt parameters, compare
examples in a learned space, or condition predictions on examples
provided at inference time.

## Practical example

A pretrained image model may be given a few labeled examples of a newly
observed product defect and use their feature similarities to classify
additional images. Results should be checked on separate examples from
the target setting.

## Common misconceptions

- Few-shot learning is not zero-shot learning; it uses a small number of
  examples.
- A few examples do not guarantee reliable coverage of a class's
  variation.
- Prompting a language model with examples is one few-shot technique,
  not the only meaning of the term.
